[7:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[7:2] To supplement our condensed consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with U.S.
[7:3] generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: Adjusted EBITDA,
[7:4] Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted net income (loss), Adjusted net income (loss) per diluted share, Free cash flow, and Adjusted
[7:5] effective tax rate (collectively the “non-GAAP financial measures”). The presentation of this financial information is not intended
[7:6] to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance
[7:7] with GAAP.
[7:8] We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision making and as a means to evaluate period-to-
[7:9] period comparisons. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information
[7:10] regarding our performance and liquidity by excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core business
[7:11] operating results or, in certain cases, may be non-cash in nature. We believe that both management and investors benefit from
[7:12] referring to these non-GAAP financial measures in assessing our performance and when planning, forecasting, and analyzing
[7:13] future periods. These non-GAAP financial measures also facilitate management’s internal comparisons to our historical
[7:14] performance and liquidity. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors both because (1) they allow for
[7:15] greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making, (2)
[7:16] certain measures are used to determine the amount of annual incentive compensation paid to our named executive officers, and
[7:17] (3) they are used by the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business.
[7:18] These non-GAAP financial measures are not measures presented in accordance with GAAP, and our use of these terms may
[7:19] vary from that of other companies, limiting their usefulness for comparison purposes. These non-GAAP financial measures are
[7:20] not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. These non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in
[7:21] that they do not reflect all of the amounts associated with the Company’s results of operations determined in accordance with
[7:22] GAAP.
[7:23] Non-GAAP financial measures exclude the certain items listed below. We believe that excluding these items from the non-GAAP
[7:24] measures facilitates comparisons to historical operating results and comparisons to peers, many of which exclude similar items.
[7:25] We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding operational performance.
[7:26] We further believe these measures are useful to investors in that they allow for greater transparency of certain line items in the
[7:27] Company’s financial statements.
[7:28] Adjusted EBITDA is defined as Net income (loss) with adjustments to reflect the addition or elimination of certain items
[7:29] including, but not limited to:
[7:30]     • Interest expense, net. Interest expense is generated primarily from interest due on outstanding debt, partially offset by
[7:31]       interest income generated from the interest earned on cash, cash equivalents, and investments;
[7:32]     • (Gain) loss on debt extinguishment, net. This is a non-cash expense that relates to extinguishments of long-term debt
[7:33]       obligations. We believe this (gain) loss does not represent recurring core business operating results of the Company;
[7:34]     • (Gain) loss on sale of business. This gain or loss relates to the sales of businesses and does not represent recurring core
[7:35]       business operating results of the Company;
[7:36]     • (Gain) loss on investments, net. This item includes realized gains and losses, unrealized gains and losses, and
[7:37]       impairment charges on debt and equity investments. The amount of gain or loss depends on the share price for
[7:38]       investments with readily determinable fair value and on observable price changes for investments without a readily
[7:39]       determinable fair value, and does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:40]     • Other (income) loss, net. This income or expense relates to other non-operating items and does not represent recurring
[7:41]       core business operating results of the Company;
[7:42]     • Income tax (benefit) expense. This benefit or expense depends on the pre-tax loss or income of the Company, statutory
[7:43]       tax rates, tax regulations, and different tax rates in various jurisdictions in which the Company operates and which the
[7:44]       Company does not have the control over;
[7:45]     • (Income) loss from equity method investments, net. This is a non-cash expense as it relates primarily to our investment in
[7:46]       OCV Fund I, LP (the “Fund”). We believe that gain or loss resulting from our equity method investment does not represent
[7:47]       core business operating results of the Company;
[7:48]     • Depreciation and amortization. This is a non-cash expense at it relates to use and associated reduction in value of certain
[7:49]       assets including equipment, fixtures, and certain capitalized internal-used software and website development costs, and
[7:50]       identifiable definite-lived intangible assets of the acquired businesses;
[7:51]     • Share-based compensation. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to awards granted under the various share-based
[7:52]       incentive plans of the Company. We view the economic cost of share-based awards to be the dilution to our share base;
[7:53]     • Acquisition, integration, and other costs. Includes adjustments to contingent consideration, lease terminations, retention
[7:54]       bonuses, other acquisition-specific items, and other costs, such as severance, third-party debt modification costs, and
[7:55]       legal settlements. These expenses do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:56]                                                                  7
[8:1]     • Disposal related costs. These are expenses associated with the disposal of certain businesses that do not represent core
[8:2]       business operating results of the Company;
[8:3]     • Lease asset impairments and other charges. These expenses are incurred in connection with impaired right-of-use
[8:4]       (“ROU”) assets of the Company. Associated expenses are comprised of insurance, utility, and other charges related to
[8:5]       assets that are no longer in use, and partially offset by the sublease income earned. These expenses do not represent
[8:6]       core business operating results of the Company; and
[8:7]     • Goodwill impairment on business. This is a non-cash expense that is recorded when the carrying value of the reporting
[8:8]       unit exceeds its fair value and does not represent core business operating results of the Company.
[8:9] Adjusted EBITDA margin is calculated by dividing Adjusted EBITDA by Total revenues.
[8:10] Adjusted net income (loss) is defined as Net income (loss) with adjustments to reflect the addition or elimination of certain
[8:11] statement of operations items including, but not limited to:
[8:12]     • Interest, net. This reflects the difference between the imputed and coupon interest expense associated with the 4.625%
[8:13]       Senior Notes and a charge that the Company determined to be penalty interest associated with the 1.75% Convertible
[8:14]       Notes in each period presented, offset in part by a certain interest income earned by the Company. These net expenses
[8:15]       do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:16]     • (Gain) loss on debt extinguishment, net. This is a non-cash expense that relates to extinguishments of long-term debt
[8:17]       obligations. We believe this gain or loss does not represent recurring core business operating results of the Company;
[8:18]     • (Gain) loss on sale of business. This gain or loss relates to the sales of businesses and does not represent recurring core
[8:19]       business operating results of the Company;
[8:20]     • (Gain) loss on investments, net. This item includes realized gains and losses, unrealized gains and losses, and
[8:21]       impairment charges on debt and equity investments. The amount of gain or loss depends on the share price for
[8:22]       investments with readily determinable fair value and on observable price changes for investments without a readily
[8:23]       determinable fair value, and does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:24]     • (Income) loss from equity method investments, net. This is a non-cash income or expense as it relates primarily to our
[8:25]       investment in the OCV Fund. We believe that gains or losses resulting from our equity method investment do not
[8:26]       represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:27]     • Amortization. Includes the amortization of patents and intangible assets that we acquired. This is a non-cash expense as it
[8:28]       primarily relates to identifiable definite-lived intangible assets of the acquired businesses. We believe that acquired
[8:29]       intangible assets represent cost incurred by the acquiree to build value prior to the acquisition and the amortization of this
[8:30]       cost does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:31]     • Share-based compensation. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to awards granted under the various incentive plans
[8:32]       of the Company. We view the economic cost of share-based awards to be the dilution to our share base;
[8:33]     • Acquisition, integration, and other costs. Includes adjustments to contingent consideration, lease terminations, retention
[8:34]       bonuses, other acquisition-specific items, and other costs, such as severance, third-party debt modification costs, and
[8:35]       legal settlements. These expenses do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:36]     • Disposal related costs. These are expenses associated with the disposal of certain businesses that do not represent core
[8:37]       business operating results of the Company;
[8:38]     • Lease asset impairments and other charges. These expenses are incurred in connection with impaired ROU assets of the
[8:39]       Company. Associated expenses are comprised of insurance, utility, and other charges related to assets that are no longer
[8:40]       in use, and partially offset by the sublease income earned. These expenses do not represent core business operating
[8:41]       results of the Company; and
[8:42]     • Goodwill impairment on business. This is a non-cash expense that is recorded when the carrying value of the reporting
[8:43]       unit exceeds its fair value and does not represent core business operating results of the Company.
[8:44] Adjusted net income (loss) per diluted share is calculated by dividing Adjusted net income (loss) by the diluted weighted
[8:45] average shares of common stock outstanding excluding the effect of convertible debt dilution.
[8:46] Free cash flow is defined as Net cash provided by operating activities, less purchases of property and equipment, plus changes
[8:47] in contingent consideration (if any).
[8:48] Adjusted effective tax rate is calculated based upon the GAAP effective tax rate with adjustments for the tax applicable to non-
[8:49] GAAP adjustments to Net income (loss), generally based upon the effective marginal tax rate of each adjustment.

[6:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[6:2] To supplement our condensed consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with U.S.
[6:3] generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: Adjusted EBITDA,
[6:4] Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted net income (loss), Adjusted net income (loss) per diluted share, Free cash flow, and Adjusted
[6:5] effective tax rate (collectively the “non-GAAP financial measures”). The presentation of this financial information is not intended
[6:6] to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance
[6:7] with GAAP.
[6:8] We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision making and as a means to evaluate period-to-
[6:9] period comparisons. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information
[6:10] regarding our performance and liquidity by excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core business
[6:11] operating results or, in certain cases, may be non-cash in nature. We believe that both management and investors benefit from
[6:12] referring to these non-GAAP financial measures in assessing our performance and when planning, forecasting, and analyzing
[6:13] future periods. These non-GAAP financial measures also facilitate management’s internal comparisons to our historical
[6:14] performance and liquidity. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors both because (1) they allow for
[6:15] greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making, (2)
[6:16] certain measures are used to determine the amount of annual incentive compensation paid to our named executive officers, and
[6:17] (3) they are used by the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business.
[6:18] These non-GAAP financial measures are not measures presented in accordance with GAAP, and our use of these terms may
[6:19] vary from that of other companies, limiting their usefulness for comparison purposes. These non-GAAP financial measures are
[6:20] not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. These non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in
[6:21] that they do not reflect all of the amounts associated with the Company’s results of operations determined in accordance with
[6:22] GAAP.
[6:23] Non-GAAP financial measures exclude the certain items listed below. We believe that excluding these items from the non-GAAP
[6:24] measures facilitates comparisons to historical operating results and comparisons to peers, many of which exclude similar items.
[6:25] We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding operational performance.
[6:26] We further believe these measures are useful to investors in that they allow for greater transparency of certain line items in the
[6:27] Company’s financial statements.
[6:28] Adjusted EBITDA is defined as Net income (loss) with adjustments to reflect the addition or elimination of certain items
[6:29] including, but not limited to:
[6:30]     • Interest expense, net. Interest expense is generated primarily from interest due on outstanding debt, partially offset by
[6:31]       interest income generated from the interest earned on cash, cash equivalents, and investments;
[6:32]     • (Gain) loss on debt extinguishment, net. This is a non-cash expense that relates to extinguishments of long-term debt
[6:33]       obligations. We believe this (gain) loss does not represent recurring core business operating results of the Company;
[6:34]     • (Gain) loss on sale of business. This gain or loss relates to the sales of businesses and does not represent recurring core
[6:35]       business operating results of the Company;
[6:36]     • Unrealized (gain) loss on short-term investments held at the reporting date, net. This is a non-cash item as it relates to the
[6:37]       change in the carrying value of our investment in Consensus depending on the share price of Consensus common stock
[6:38]       and does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[6:39]     • (Gain) loss on investments, net. This item relates to the disposition of a portion of our investment in Consensus. The
[6:40]       amount of gain or loss depends on the share price of Consensus common stock and does not represent core business
[6:41]       operating results of the Company;
[6:42]     • Other (income) loss, net. This income or expense relates to other non-operating items and does not represent recurring
[6:43]       core business operating results of the Company;
[6:44]     • Income tax (benefit) expense. This benefit or expense depends on the pre-tax loss or income of the Company, statutory
[6:45]       tax rates, tax regulations, and different tax rates in various jurisdictions in which the Company operates and which the
[6:46]       Company does not have the control over;
[6:47]     • (Income) loss from equity method investments, net. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to our investment in OCV
[6:48]       Fund I, LP (the “Fund”). We believe that gain or loss resulting from our equity method investment does not represent core
[6:49]       business operating results of the Company;
[6:50]     • Depreciation and amortization. This is a non-cash expense at it relates to use and associated reduction in value of certain
[6:51]       assets including equipment, fixtures, and certain capitalized internal-used software and website development costs, and
[6:52]       identifiable definite-lived intangible assets of the acquired businesses;
[6:53]     • Share-based compensation. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to awards granted under the various share-based
[6:54]       incentive plans of the Company. We view the economic cost of share-based awards to be the dilution to our share base;
[6:55]                                                                  6
[7:1]     • Acquisition, integration, and other costs. Includes adjustments to contingent consideration, lease terminations, retention
[7:2]       bonuses, other acquisition-specific items, and other costs, such as severance, third-party debt modification costs, and
[7:3]       legal settlements. These expenses do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:4]     • Disposal related costs. These are expenses associated with the disposal of certain businesses that do not represent core
[7:5]       business operating results of the Company;
[7:6]     • Lease asset impairments and other charges. These expenses are incurred in connection with impaired right-of-use
[7:7]       (“ROU”) assets of the Company. Associated expenses are comprised of insurance, utility, and other charges related to
[7:8]       assets that are no longer in use, and partially offset by the sublease income earned. These expenses do not represent
[7:9]       core business operating results of the Company; and
[7:10]     • Goodwill impairment on business. This is a non-cash expense that is recorded when the carrying value of the reporting
[7:11]       unit exceeds its fair value and does not represent core business operating results of the Company.
[7:12] Adjusted EBITDA margin is calculated by dividing Adjusted EBITDA by Total revenues.
[7:13] Adjusted net income (loss) is defined as Net income (loss) with adjustments to reflect the addition or elimination of certain
[7:14] statement of operations items including, but not limited to:
[7:15]     • Interest, net. This reflects the difference between the imputed and coupon interest expense associated with the 4.625%
[7:16]       Senior Notes and a charge that the Company determined to be penalty interest associated with the 1.75% Convertible
[7:17]       Notes in each period presented, offset in part by a certain interest income earned by the Company. These net expenses
[7:18]       do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:19]     • (Gain) loss on debt extinguishment, net. This is a non-cash expense that relates to extinguishments of long-term debt
[7:20]       obligations. We believe this gain or loss does not represent recurring core business operating results of the Company;
[7:21]     • (Gain) loss on sale of business. This gain or loss relates to the sales of businesses and does not represent recurring core
[7:22]       business operating results of the Company;
[7:23]     • Unrealized (gain) loss on short-term investments held at the reporting date, net. This is a non-cash item as it relates to the
[7:24]       change in the carrying value of our investment in Consensus depending on the share price of Consensus common stock
[7:25]       and does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:26]     • (Gain) loss on investments, net. This item relates to the disposition of a portion of our investment in Consensus. The
[7:27]       amount of gain or loss depends on the share price of Consensus common stock and does not represent core business
[7:28]       operating results of the Company;
[7:29]     • (Income) loss from equity method investments, net. This is a non-cash income or expense as it relates to our investment
[7:30]       in the OCV Fund. We believe that gains or losses resulting from our equity method investment do not represent core
[7:31]       business operating results of the Company;
[7:32]     • Amortization. Includes the amortization of patents and intangible assets that we acquired. This is a non-cash expense as it
[7:33]       primarily relates to identifiable definite-lived intangible assets of the acquired businesses. We believe that acquired
[7:34]       intangible assets represent cost incurred by the acquiree to build value prior to the acquisition and the amortization of this
[7:35]       cost does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:36]     • Share-based compensation. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to awards granted under the various incentive plans
[7:37]       of the Company. We view the economic cost of share-based awards to be the dilution to our share base;
[7:38]     • Acquisition, integration, and other costs. Includes adjustments to contingent consideration, lease terminations, retention
[7:39]       bonuses, other acquisition-specific items, and other costs, such as severance, third-party debt modification costs, and
[7:40]       legal settlements. These expenses do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:41]     • Disposal related costs. These are expenses associated with the disposal of certain businesses that do not represent core
[7:42]       business operating results of the Company;
[7:43]     • Lease asset impairments and other charges. These expenses are incurred in connection with impaired ROU assets of the
[7:44]       Company. Associated expenses comprised of insurance, utility, and other charges related to assets that are no longer in
[7:45]       use, and partially offset by the sublease income earned. These expenses do not represent core business operating results
[7:46]       of the Company; and
[7:47]     • Goodwill impairment on business. This is a non-cash expense that is recorded when the carrying value of the reporting
[7:48]       unit exceeds its fair value and does not represent core business operating results of the Company.
[7:49] Adjusted net income (loss) per diluted share is calculated by dividing Adjusted net income (loss) by the diluted weighted
[7:50] average shares of common stock outstanding excluding the effect of convertible debt dilution.

[7:52] in contingent consideration (if any).

[7:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[7:2] To supplement our condensed consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with U.S.
[7:3] generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”), we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: Adjusted EBITDA,
[7:4] Adjusted EBITDA margin, Adjusted net income (loss), Adjusted net income (loss) per diluted share, Free cash flow, and Adjusted
[7:5] effective tax rate (collectively the “non-GAAP financial measures”). The presentation of this financial information is not intended
[7:6] to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, the financial information prepared and presented in accordance
[7:7] with GAAP.
[7:8] We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision making and as a means to evaluate period-to-
[7:9] period comparisons. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information
[7:10] regarding our performance and liquidity by excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core business
[7:11] operating results or, in certain cases, may be non-cash in nature. We believe that both management and investors benefit from
[7:12] referring to these non-GAAP financial measures in assessing our performance and when planning, forecasting, and analyzing
[7:13] future periods. These non-GAAP financial measures also facilitate management’s internal comparisons to our historical
[7:14] performance and liquidity. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors both because (1) they allow for
[7:15] greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management in its financial and operational decision-making, (2)
[7:16] certain measures are used to determine the amount of annual incentive compensation paid to our named executive officers, and
[7:17] (3) they are used by the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business.
[7:18] These non-GAAP financial measures are not measures presented in accordance with GAAP, and our use of these terms may
[7:19] vary from that of other companies, limiting their usefulness for comparison purposes. These non-GAAP financial measures are
[7:20] not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. These non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in
[7:21] that they do not reflect all of the amounts associated with the Company’s results of operations determined in accordance with
[7:22] GAAP.
[7:23] Non-GAAP financial measures exclude the certain items listed below. We believe that excluding these items from the non-GAAP
[7:24] measures facilitates comparisons to historical operating results and comparisons to peers, many of which exclude similar items.
[7:25] We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information regarding operational performance.
[7:26] We further believe these measures are useful to investors in that they allow for greater transparency of certain line items in the
[7:27] Company’s financial statements.
[7:28] Adjusted EBITDA is defined as Net income (loss) with adjustments to reflect the addition or elimination of certain items
[7:29] including, but not limited to:
[7:30]     • Interest expense, net. Interest expense is generated primarily from interest due on outstanding debt, partially offset by
[7:31]       interest income generated from the interest earned on cash, cash equivalents, and investments;
[7:32]     • (Gain) loss on debt extinguishment, net. This is a non-cash expense that relates to extinguishments of long-term debt
[7:33]       obligations. We believe this (gain) loss does not represent recurring core business operating results of the Company;
[7:34]     • (Gain) loss on sale of business. This gain or loss relates to the sales of businesses and does not represent recurring core
[7:35]       business operating results of the Company;
[7:36]     • (Gain) loss on investments, net. This item includes realized gains and losses, unrealized gains and losses, and
[7:37]       impairment charges on debt and equity investments. The amount of gain or loss depends on the share price for
[7:38]       investments with readily determinable fair value and on observable price changes for investments without a readily
[7:39]       determinable fair value, and does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:40]     • Other (income) loss, net. This income or expense relates to other non-operating items and does not represent recurring
[7:41]       core business operating results of the Company;
[7:42]     • Income tax (benefit) expense. This benefit or expense depends on the pre-tax loss or income of the Company, statutory
[7:43]       tax rates, tax regulations, and different tax rates in various jurisdictions in which the Company operates and which the
[7:44]       Company does not have the control over;
[7:45]     • (Income) loss from equity method investments, net. This is a non-cash expense as it relates primarily to our investment in
[7:46]       OCV Fund I, LP (the “Fund”). We believe that gain or loss resulting from our equity method investment does not represent
[7:47]       core business operating results of the Company;
[7:48]     • Depreciation and amortization. This is a non-cash expense at it relates to use and associated reduction in value of certain
[7:49]       assets including equipment, fixtures, and certain capitalized internal-used software and website development costs, and
[7:50]       identifiable definite-lived intangible assets of the acquired businesses;
[7:51]     • Share-based compensation. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to awards granted under the various share-based
[7:52]       incentive plans of the Company. We view the economic cost of share-based awards to be the dilution to our share base;
[7:53]     • Acquisition, integration, and other costs. Includes adjustments to contingent consideration, lease terminations, retention
[7:54]       bonuses, other acquisition-specific items, and other costs, such as severance, third-party debt modification costs, and
[7:55]       legal settlements. These expenses do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[7:56]                                                                  7
[8:1]     • Disposal related costs. These are expenses associated with the disposal of certain businesses that do not represent core
[8:2]       business operating results of the Company;
[8:3]     • Lease asset impairments and other charges. These expenses are incurred in connection with impaired right-of-use
[8:4]       (“ROU”) assets of the Company. Associated expenses are comprised of insurance, utility, and other charges related to
[8:5]       assets that are no longer in use, and partially offset by the sublease income earned. These expenses do not represent
[8:6]       core business operating results of the Company; and
[8:7]     • Goodwill impairment on business. This is a non-cash expense that is recorded when the carrying value of the reporting
[8:8]       unit exceeds its fair value and does not represent core business operating results of the Company.
[8:9] Adjusted EBITDA margin is calculated by dividing Adjusted EBITDA by Total revenues.
[8:10] Adjusted net income (loss) is defined as Net income (loss) with adjustments to reflect the addition or elimination of certain
[8:11] statement of operations items including, but not limited to:
[8:12]     • Interest, net. This reflects the difference between the imputed and coupon interest expense associated with the 4.625%
[8:13]       Senior Notes and a charge that the Company determined to be penalty interest associated with the 1.75% Convertible
[8:14]       Notes in each period presented, offset in part by a certain interest income earned by the Company. These net expenses
[8:15]       do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:16]     • (Gain) loss on debt extinguishment, net. This is a non-cash expense that relates to extinguishments of long-term debt
[8:17]       obligations. We believe this gain or loss does not represent recurring core business operating results of the Company;
[8:18]     • (Gain) loss on sale of business. This gain or loss relates to the sales of businesses and does not represent recurring core
[8:19]       business operating results of the Company;
[8:20]     • (Gain) loss on investments, net. This item includes realized gains and losses, unrealized gains and losses, and
[8:21]       impairment charges on debt and equity investments. The amount of gain or loss depends on the share price for
[8:22]       investments with readily determinable fair value and on observable price changes for investments without a readily
[8:23]       determinable fair value, and does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:24]     • (Income) loss from equity method investments, net. This is a non-cash income or expense as it relates primarily to our
[8:25]       investment in the OCV Fund. We believe that gains or losses resulting from our equity method investment do not
[8:26]       represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:27]     • Amortization. Includes the amortization of patents and intangible assets that we acquired. This is a non-cash expense as it
[8:28]       primarily relates to identifiable definite-lived intangible assets of the acquired businesses. We believe that acquired
[8:29]       intangible assets represent cost incurred by the acquiree to build value prior to the acquisition and the amortization of this
[8:30]       cost does not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:31]     • Share-based compensation. This is a non-cash expense as it relates to awards granted under the various incentive plans
[8:32]       of the Company. We view the economic cost of share-based awards to be the dilution to our share base;
[8:33]     • Acquisition, integration, and other costs. Includes adjustments to contingent consideration, lease terminations, retention
[8:34]       bonuses, other acquisition-specific items, and other costs, such as severance, third-party debt modification costs, and
[8:35]       legal settlements. These expenses do not represent core business operating results of the Company;
[8:36]     • Disposal related costs. These are expenses associated with the disposal of certain businesses that do not represent core
[8:37]       business operating results of the Company;
[8:38]     • Lease asset impairments and other charges. These expenses are incurred in connection with impaired ROU assets of the
[8:39]       Company. Associated expenses are comprised of insurance, utility, and other charges related to assets that are no longer
[8:40]       in use, and partially offset by the sublease income earned. These expenses do not represent core business operating
[8:41]       results of the Company; and
[8:42]     • Goodwill impairment on business. This is a non-cash expense that is recorded when the carrying value of the reporting
[8:43]       unit exceeds its fair value and does not represent core business operating results of the Company.
[8:44] Adjusted net income (loss) per diluted share is calculated by dividing Adjusted net income (loss) by the diluted weighted
[8:45] average shares of common stock outstanding excluding the effect of convertible debt dilution.
[8:46] Free cash flow is defined as Net cash provided by operating activities, less purchases of property and equipment, plus changes
[8:47] in contingent consideration (if any).
[8:48] Adjusted effective tax rate is calculated based upon the GAAP effective tax rate with adjustments for the tax applicable to non-
[8:49] GAAP adjustments to Net income (loss), generally based upon the effective marginal tax rate of each adjustment.

[7:1] We believe it is useful to exclude non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization and share-based compensation

[7:4] interest income (expense), net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; and litigation matters and
[7:5] other items which are not components of our core business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude severance and exit
[7:6] costs because these expenses represent temporary initiatives to realign resources and enhance operational efficiency, which are
[7:7] not components of our core business operations. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as a financial measure and you should not
[7:8] consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are:
[7:9]     •    although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized may have to
[7:10]          be replaced in the future and adjusted EBITDA does not reflect capital expenditure requirements for such replacements
[7:11]          or for new capital expenditures;
[7:12]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect share-based compensation and related taxes. Share-based compensation has been,
[7:13]          and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a recurring expense in our business and an important part of our
[7:14]          compensation strategy;
[7:15]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest income (expense), net; or changes in, or cash requirements for, our working
[7:16]          capital;
[7:17]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect transaction related costs and other items which are either not representative of our
[7:18]          underlying operations or are incremental costs that result from an actual or planned transaction or initiative and include

[7:22]     •    other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate adjusted EBITDA differently, which reduces its
[7:23]          usefulness as a comparative measure.

[6:43] Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin
[6:44] To provide investors with additional information regarding our financial results, we have disclosed in this earnings release
[6:45] adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure that we calculate as net income excluding depreciation and amortization;
[6:46] share-based compensation expense and related taxes; income tax provision (benefit); interest income (expense), net; transaction
[6:47] related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; severance and exit costs; and litigation matters and other items that
[6:48] we do not consider representative of our underlying operations. We have provided a reconciliation below of adjusted EBITDA
[6:49] to net income, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.
[6:50] We have included adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin in this earnings release because each is a key measure used
[6:51] by our management and board of directors to evaluate our operating performance, generate future operating plans and make
[6:52] strategic decisions regarding the allocation of capital. In particular, the exclusion of certain expenses in calculating adjusted
[6:53] EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin facilitates operating performance comparability across reporting periods by removing
[6:54] the effect of non-cash expenses and certain variable charges. Accordingly, we believe that adjusted EBITDA and adjusted
[6:55] EBITDA margin provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the
[6:56] same manner as our management and board of directors.
[7:1] We believe it is useful to exclude non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization and share-based compensation
[7:2] expense from our adjusted EBITDA because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to
[7:3] the underlying performance of our business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude income tax provision (benefit);
[7:4] interest income (expense), net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; and litigation matters and
[7:5] other items which are not components of our core business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude severance and exit
[7:6] costs because these expenses represent temporary initiatives to realign resources and enhance operational efficiency, which are
[7:7] not components of our core business operations. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as a financial measure and you should not
[7:8] consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are:
[7:9]     •    although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized may have to
[7:10]          be replaced in the future and adjusted EBITDA does not reflect capital expenditure requirements for such replacements
[7:11]          or for new capital expenditures;
[7:12]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect share-based compensation and related taxes. Share-based compensation has been,
[7:13]          and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a recurring expense in our business and an important part of our
[7:14]          compensation strategy;
[7:15]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest income (expense), net; or changes in, or cash requirements for, our working
[7:16]          capital;
[7:17]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect transaction related costs and other items which are either not representative of our
[7:18]          underlying operations or are incremental costs that result from an actual or planned transaction or initiative and include
[7:19]          changes in the fair value of equity warrants, severance and exit costs, litigation matters, integration consulting fees,
[7:20]          internal salaries and wages (to the extent the individuals are assigned full-time to integration and transformation
[7:21]          activities) and certain costs related to integrating and converging IT systems; and
[7:22]     •    other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate adjusted EBITDA differently, which reduces its
[7:23]          usefulness as a comparative measure.
[7:24] Because of these limitations, you should consider adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin alongside other financial
[7:25] performance measures, including various cash flow metrics, net income, net margin, and our other GAAP results.

[6:35] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[6:36] Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin
[6:37] To provide investors with additional information regarding our financial results, we have disclosed in this earnings release
[6:38] adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure that we calculate as net income (loss) excluding depreciation and
[6:39] amortization; share-based compensation expense and related taxes; income tax provision (benefit); interest income (expense),
[6:40] net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; severance and exit costs; and litigation matters and
[6:41] other items that we do not consider representative of our underlying operations. We have provided a reconciliation below of
[6:42] adjusted EBITDA to net income (loss), the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.
[6:43] We have included adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin in this earnings release because each is a key measure used
[6:44] by our management and board of directors to evaluate our operating performance, generate future operating plans and make
[6:45] strategic decisions regarding the allocation of capital. In particular, the exclusion of certain expenses in calculating adjusted
[6:46] EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin facilitates operating performance comparability across reporting periods by removing
[6:47] the effect of non-cash expenses and certain variable charges. Accordingly, we believe that adjusted EBITDA and adjusted
[6:48] EBITDA margin provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the
[6:49] same manner as our management and board of directors.
[7:1] We believe it is useful to exclude non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization and share-based compensation
[7:2] expense from our adjusted EBITDA because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to
[7:3] the underlying performance of our business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude income tax provision (benefit);
[7:4] interest income (expense), net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; and litigation matters and
[7:5] other items which are not components of our core business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude severance and exit
[7:6] costs because these expenses represent temporary initiatives to realign resources and enhance operational efficiency, which are
[7:7] not components of our core business operations. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as a financial measure and you should not
[7:8] consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are:
[7:9]     •    although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized may have to
[7:10]          be replaced in the future and adjusted EBITDA does not reflect capital expenditure requirements for such replacements
[7:11]          or for new capital expenditures;
[7:12]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect share-based compensation and related taxes. Share-based compensation has been,
[7:13]          and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a recurring expense in our business and an important part of our
[7:14]          compensation strategy;
[7:15]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest income (expense), net; or changes in, or cash requirements for, our working
[7:16]          capital;
[7:17]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect transaction related costs and other items which are either not representative of our
[7:18]          underlying operations or are incremental costs that result from an actual or planned transaction or initiative and include
[7:19]          changes in the fair value of equity warrants, severance and exit costs, litigation matters, integration consulting fees,
[7:20]          internal salaries and wages (to the extent the individuals are assigned full-time to integration and transformation
[7:21]          activities) and certain costs related to integrating and converging IT systems; and
[7:22]     •    other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate adjusted EBITDA differently, which reduces its
[7:23]          usefulness as a comparative measure.
[7:24] Because of these limitations, you should consider adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin alongside other financial
[7:25] performance measures, including various cash flow metrics, net income (loss), net margin, and our other GAAP results.

[6:40] net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; severance and exit costs; and litigation matters and

[6:45] strategic decisions regarding the allocation of capital. In particular, the exclusion of certain expenses in calculating adjusted
[6:46] EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin facilitates operating performance comparability across reporting periods by removing
[6:47] the effect of non-cash expenses and certain variable charges. Accordingly, we believe that adjusted EBITDA and adjusted
[6:48] EBITDA margin provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the
[6:49] same manner as our management and board of directors.
[7:1] We believe it is useful to exclude non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization and share-based compensation
[7:2] expense from our adjusted EBITDA because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to
[7:3] the underlying performance of our business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude income tax provision (benefit);
[7:4] interest income (expense), net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; and litigation matters and
[7:5] other items which are not components of our core business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude severance and exit
[7:6] costs because these expenses represent temporary initiatives to realign resources and enhance operational efficiency, which are
[7:7] not components of our core business operations. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as a financial measure and you should not
[7:8] consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are:
[7:9]     •    although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized may have to
[7:10]          be replaced in the future and adjusted EBITDA does not reflect capital expenditure requirements for such replacements
[7:11]          or for new capital expenditures;
[7:12]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect share-based compensation and related taxes. Share-based compensation has been,
[7:13]          and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a recurring expense in our business and an important part of our
[7:14]          compensation strategy;
[7:15]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest income (expense), net; or changes in, or cash requirements for, our working
[7:16]          capital;
[7:17]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect transaction related costs and other items which are either not representative of our
[7:18]          underlying operations or are incremental costs that result from an actual or planned transaction or initiative and include
[7:19]          changes in the fair value of equity warrants, severance and exit costs, litigation matters, integration consulting fees,
[7:20]          internal salaries and wages (to the extent the individuals are assigned full-time to integration and transformation
[7:21]          activities) and certain costs related to integrating and converging IT systems; and
[7:22]     •    other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate adjusted EBITDA differently, which reduces its
[7:23]          usefulness as a comparative measure.
[7:24] Because of these limitations, you should consider adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin alongside other financial
[7:25] performance measures, including various cash flow metrics, net income (loss), net margin, and our other GAAP results.

[6:42] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[6:43] Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin
[6:44] To provide investors with additional information regarding our financial results, we have disclosed in this earnings release
[6:45] adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure that we calculate as net income excluding depreciation and amortization;
[6:46] share-based compensation expense and related taxes; income tax provision (benefit); interest income (expense), net; transaction
[6:47] related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; severance and exit costs; and litigation matters and other items that
[6:48] we do not consider representative of our underlying operations. We have provided a reconciliation below of adjusted EBITDA
[6:49] to net income, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.
[6:50] We have included adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin in this earnings release because each is a key measure used
[6:51] by our management and board of directors to evaluate our operating performance, generate future operating plans and make
[6:52] strategic decisions regarding the allocation of capital. In particular, the exclusion of certain expenses in calculating adjusted
[6:53] EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin facilitates operating performance comparability across reporting periods by removing
[6:54] the effect of non-cash expenses and certain variable charges. Accordingly, we believe that adjusted EBITDA and adjusted
[6:55] EBITDA margin provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the
[6:56] same manner as our management and board of directors.
[7:1] We believe it is useful to exclude non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization and share-based compensation
[7:2] expense from our adjusted EBITDA because the amount of such expenses in any specific period may not directly correlate to
[7:3] the underlying performance of our business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude income tax provision (benefit);
[7:4] interest income (expense), net; transaction related costs; changes in the fair value of equity warrants; and litigation matters and
[7:5] other items which are not components of our core business operations. We believe it is useful to exclude severance and exit
[7:6] costs because these expenses represent temporary initiatives to realign resources and enhance operational efficiency, which are
[7:7] not components of our core business operations. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as a financial measure and you should not
[7:8] consider it in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Some of these limitations are:
[7:9]     •    although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized may have to
[7:10]          be replaced in the future and adjusted EBITDA does not reflect capital expenditure requirements for such replacements
[7:11]          or for new capital expenditures;
[7:12]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect share-based compensation and related taxes. Share-based compensation has been,
[7:13]          and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a recurring expense in our business and an important part of our
[7:14]          compensation strategy;
[7:15]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect interest income (expense), net; or changes in, or cash requirements for, our working
[7:16]          capital;
[7:17]     •    adjusted EBITDA does not reflect transaction related costs and other items which are either not representative of our
[7:18]          underlying operations or are incremental costs that result from an actual or planned transaction or initiative and include
[7:19]          changes in the fair value of equity warrants, severance and exit costs, litigation matters, integration consulting fees,
[7:20]          internal salaries and wages (to the extent the individuals are assigned full-time to integration and transformation
[7:21]          activities) and certain costs related to integrating and converging IT systems; and
[7:22]     •    other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate adjusted EBITDA differently, which reduces its
[7:23]          usefulness as a comparative measure.
[7:24] Because of these limitations, you should consider adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin alongside other financial
[7:25] performance measures, including various cash flow metrics, net income, net margin, and our other GAAP results.

[1:12] results reflect the operational improvements that we have been focused on all year, and demonstrate the strength of
[1:13] our margin profile in a difficult environment,” said Laura Alber, President and Chief Executive Officer.

[4:4] Barn Teen, West Elm, Williams Sonoma Home, Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, and GreenRow — are marketed

[4:7] brands. We operate in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Canada, Australia and the United Kingdom, offer international shipping to
[4:8] customers worldwide, and have unaffiliated franchisees that operate stores in the Middle East, the Philippines, Mexico,

[4:10] industry with our values-based culture and commitment to achieving our sustainability goals. Our company is Good By

[7:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[7:2]       This press release and the accompanying tables contain the non-GAAP financial measure bookings, Adjusted EBITDA,
[7:3] and free cash flow.
[7:4]      We use this non-GAAP financial information to evaluate our ongoing operations and for internal planning and forecasting
[7:5] purposes. We believe that this non-GAAP financial information may be helpful to investors because it provides consistency and
[7:6] comparability with past financial performance.
[7:7]        Bookings is defined as revenue plus the change in deferred revenue during the period and other non-cash adjustments.
[7:8] Substantially all of our bookings are generated from sales of virtual currency, which can ultimately be converted to virtual items
[7:9] on the Roblox Platform. Sales of virtual currency reflected as bookings include one-time purchases and monthly subscriptions
[7:10] purchased via payment processors or through prepaid cards. Bookings also include an insignificant amount from advertising
[7:11] and licensing arrangements. We believe bookings provide a timelier indication of trends in our operating results that are not
[7:12] necessarily reflected in our revenue as a result of the fact that we recognize the majority of revenue over the estimated average
[7:13] lifetime of a paying user. The change in deferred revenue constitutes the vast majority of the reconciling difference from
[7:14] revenue to bookings. By removing these non-cash adjustments, we are able to measure and monitor our business performance
[7:15] based on the timing of actual transactions with our users and the cash that is generated from these transactions. Adjusted
[7:16] EBITDA represents our GAAP consolidated net loss, excluding interest income, interest expense, other income/(expense),
[7:17] provision for/(benefit from) income taxes, depreciation and amortization expense, stock-based compensation expense, and

[1:9]        •   Revenue was $919.0 million, up 29% year-over-year.
[1:10]        •   Bookings1 were $1,128.5 million, up 34% year-over-year.
[1:11]        •   Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $239.3 million, while consolidated net loss was $240.4 million.

[1:15]            cash flow1 was $218.0 million, up 266% year-over-year.
[1:16]        •   Average Daily Active Users (“DAUs”) were 88.9 million, up 27% year-over-year.

[1:18]            payer was $19.70.

[1:22]            $2.9 billion.

[1:26] our continued innovation and focus on safety will drive long-term value for our shareholders and the broader Roblox
[1:27] community,” said David Baszucki, founder and CEO of Roblox.

[7:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[7:2]       This press release and the accompanying tables contain the non-GAAP financial measure bookings, Adjusted EBITDA,
[7:3] and free cash flow.
[7:4]       We use this non-GAAP financial information to evaluate our ongoing operations and for internal planning and
[7:5] forecasting purposes. We believe that this non-GAAP financial information may be helpful to investors because it provides
[7:6] consistency and comparability with past financial performance.
[7:7]        Bookings is defined as revenue plus the change in deferred revenue during the period and other non-cash adjustments.
[7:8] Substantially all of our bookings are generated from sales of virtual currency, which can ultimately be converted to virtual items
[7:9] on the Roblox Platform. Sales of virtual currency reflected as bookings include one-time purchases and monthly subscriptions
[7:10] purchased via payment processors or through prepaid cards. Bookings also include an insignificant amount from advertising
[7:11] and licensing arrangements. We believe bookings provide a timelier indication of trends in our operating results that are not
[7:12] necessarily reflected in our revenue as a result of the fact that we recognize the majority of revenue over the estimated average
[7:13] lifetime of a paying user. The change in deferred revenue constitutes the vast majority of the reconciling difference from
[7:14] revenue to bookings. By removing these non-cash adjustments, we are able to measure and monitor our business performance
[7:15] based on the timing of actual transactions with our users and the cash that is generated from these transactions. Adjusted
[7:16] EBITDA represents our GAAP consolidated net loss, excluding interest income, interest expense, other income/(expense),
[7:17] provision for/(benefit from) income taxes, depreciation and amortization expense, stock-based compensation expense, and
[7:18] certain other nonrecurring adjustments. We believe that, when considered together with reported GAAP amounts, Adjusted
[7:19] EBITDA is useful to investors and management in understanding our ongoing operations and ongoing operating trends. Our
[7:20] definition of Adjusted EBITDA may differ from the definition used by other companies and therefore comparability may be
[7:21] limited. Free cash flow represents the net cash and cash equivalents provided by operating activities less purchases of property,
[7:22] equipment, and intangible assets acquired through asset acquisitions. We believe that free cash flow is a useful indicator of our
[7:23] unit economics and liquidity that provides information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated from
[7:24] our core operations that, after the purchases of property, equipment, and intangible assets acquired through asset acquisitions,
[7:25] can be used for strategic initiatives.
[7:26]       Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized
[7:27] meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition,
[7:28] other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures differently
[7:29] or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial
[7:30] information as a tool for comparison. As a result, our non-GAAP financial information is presented for supplemental
[7:31] informational purposes only and should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for financial information
[7:32] presented in accordance with GAAP.
[7:33]        Reconciliation tables of the most comparable GAAP financial measure to the non-GAAP financial measure used in this
[7:34] press release are included below. We encourage investors and others to review our business, results of operations, and financial
[7:35] information in their entirety, not to rely on any single financial measure, and to view these non-GAAP measures in conjunction

[7:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[7:2]       This press release and the accompanying tables contain the non-GAAP financial measure bookings, Adjusted EBITDA,
[7:3] and free cash flow.
[7:4]      We use this non-GAAP financial information to evaluate our ongoing operations and for internal planning and forecasting
[7:5] purposes. We believe that this non-GAAP financial information may be helpful to investors because it provides consistency and
[7:6] comparability with past financial performance.
[7:7]        Bookings is defined as revenue plus the change in deferred revenue during the period and other non-cash adjustments.
[7:8] Substantially all of our bookings are generated from sales of virtual currency, which can ultimately be converted to virtual items
[7:9] on the Roblox Platform. Sales of virtual currency reflected as bookings include one-time purchases and monthly subscriptions
[7:10] purchased via payment processors or through prepaid cards. Bookings also include an insignificant amount from advertising
[7:11] and licensing arrangements. We believe bookings provide a timelier indication of trends in our operating results that are not
[7:12] necessarily reflected in our revenue as a result of the fact that we recognize the majority of revenue over the estimated average
[7:13] lifetime of a paying user. The change in deferred revenue constitutes the vast majority of the reconciling difference from
[7:14] revenue to bookings. By removing these non-cash adjustments, we are able to measure and monitor our business performance
[7:15] based on the timing of actual transactions with our users and the cash that is generated from these transactions. Adjusted
[7:16] EBITDA represents our GAAP consolidated net loss, excluding interest income, interest expense, other income/(expense),
[7:17] provision for/(benefit from) income taxes, depreciation and amortization expense, stock-based compensation expense, and
[7:18] certain other nonrecurring adjustments. We believe that, when considered together with reported GAAP amounts, Adjusted
[7:19] EBITDA is useful to investors and management in understanding our ongoing operations and ongoing operating trends. Our
[7:20] definition of Adjusted EBITDA may differ from the definition used by other companies and therefore comparability may be
[7:21] limited. Free cash flow represents the net cash and cash equivalents provided by operating activities less purchases of property,
[7:22] equipment, and intangible assets acquired through asset acquisitions. We believe that free cash flow is a useful indicator of our
[7:23] unit economics and liquidity that provides information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated from
[7:24] our core operations that, after the purchases of property, equipment, and intangible assets acquired through asset acquisitions,
[7:25] can be used for strategic initiatives.
[7:26]       Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized
[7:27] meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition,
[7:28] other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures differently
[7:29] or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial
[7:30] information as a tool for comparison. As a result, our non-GAAP financial information is presented for supplemental
[7:31] informational purposes only and should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for financial information
[7:32] presented in accordance with GAAP.
[7:33]        Reconciliation tables of the most comparable GAAP financial measure to the non-GAAP financial measure used in this
[7:34] press release are included below. We encourage investors and others to review our business, results of operations, and financial
[7:35] information in their entirety, not to rely on any single financial measure, and to view these non-GAAP measures in conjunction

[1:4] SAN MATEO, Calif., October 31, 2024 - Roblox Corporation (NYSE: RBLX), a global platform bringing millions of people
[1:5] together through shared experiences, released its third quarter 2024 financial and operational results and issued its fourth
[1:6] quarter and updated full year 2024 guidance today. Separately, Roblox posted a letter to shareholders and supplemental
[1:7] materials on the Roblox investor relations website at ir.roblox.com.
[1:8] Third Quarter 2024 Financial, Operational, and Liquidity Highlights
[1:9]        •   Revenue was $919.0 million, up 29% year-over-year.
[1:10]        •   Bookings1 were $1,128.5 million, up 34% year-over-year.
[1:11]        •   Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $239.3 million, while consolidated net loss was $240.4 million.
[1:12]        •   Adjusted EBITDA1 was $55.0 million, which excludes adjustments for increases in deferred revenue and deferred cost
[1:13]            of revenue of $216.3 million and $(47.9) million, respectively, or a total change in deferred of $168.4 million.
[1:14]        •   Net cash and cash equivalents provided by operating activities was $247.4 million, up 120% year-over-year, while free
[1:15]            cash flow1 was $218.0 million, up 266% year-over-year.
[1:16]        •   Average Daily Active Users (“DAUs”) were 88.9 million, up 27% year-over-year.
[1:17]        •   Average monthly unique payers were 19.1 million, up 30% year-over-year, and average bookings per monthly unique
[1:18]            payer was $19.70.
[1:19]        •   Hours engaged were 20.7 billion, up 29% year-over-year.
[1:20]        •   Average bookings per DAU was $12.70, up 6% year-over-year.
[1:21]        •   Cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, and long-term investments totaled $3.9 billion; net liquidity2 was
[1:22]            $2.9 billion.
[1:23] “Roblox’s exceptional Q3 results demonstrate the strength of our platform and the effectiveness of our growth strategies. We’re
[1:24] particularly proud of the progress we’ve made in empowering creators, fostering social connections, and expanding our global
[1:25] reach. As we look ahead, we remain committed to building the world’s largest social platform for play, and we’re confident that
[1:26] our continued innovation and focus on safety will drive long-term value for our shareholders and the broader Roblox
[1:27] community,” said David Baszucki, founder and CEO of Roblox.
[1:28] “In the third quarter of 2024, our key financial and operating metrics grew at high rates and in all cases were above the
[1:29] guidance we delivered on our Q2 2024 earnings call with significant year-over-year growth in revenue of 29%, bookings of
[1:30] 34%, DAUs of 27% and Hours engaged of 29%,” said Michael Guthrie, chief financial officer of Roblox.

[7:10] purchased via payment processors or through prepaid cards. Bookings also include an insignificant amount from advertising
[7:11] and licensing arrangements. We believe bookings provide a timelier indication of trends in our operating results that are not
[7:12] necessarily reflected in our revenue as a result of the fact that we recognize the majority of revenue over the estimated average
[7:13] lifetime of a paying user. The change in deferred revenue constitutes the vast majority of the reconciling difference from
[7:14] revenue to bookings. By removing these non-cash adjustments, we are able to measure and monitor our business performance
[7:15] based on the timing of actual transactions with our users and the cash that is generated from these transactions. Adjusted

[7:1] Non-GAAP Financial Measures
[7:2]       This press release and the accompanying tables contain the non-GAAP financial measure bookings, Adjusted EBITDA,
[7:3] and free cash flow.
[7:4]      We use this non-GAAP financial information to evaluate our ongoing operations and for internal planning and forecasting
[7:5] purposes. We believe that this non-GAAP financial information may be helpful to investors because it provides consistency and
[7:6] comparability with past financial performance.
[7:7]        Bookings is defined as revenue plus the change in deferred revenue during the period and other non-cash adjustments.
[7:8] Substantially all of our bookings are generated from sales of virtual currency, which can ultimately be converted to virtual items
[7:9] on the Roblox Platform. Sales of virtual currency reflected as bookings include one-time purchases and monthly subscriptions
[7:10] purchased via payment processors or through prepaid cards. Bookings also include an insignificant amount from advertising
[7:11] and licensing arrangements. We believe bookings provide a timelier indication of trends in our operating results that are not
[7:12] necessarily reflected in our revenue as a result of the fact that we recognize the majority of revenue over the estimated average
[7:13] lifetime of a paying user. The change in deferred revenue constitutes the vast majority of the reconciling difference from
[7:14] revenue to bookings. By removing these non-cash adjustments, we are able to measure and monitor our business performance
[7:15] based on the timing of actual transactions with our users and the cash that is generated from these transactions. Adjusted
[7:16] EBITDA represents our GAAP consolidated net loss, excluding interest income, interest expense, other income/(expense),
[7:17] provision for/(benefit from) income taxes, depreciation and amortization expense, stock-based compensation expense, and
[7:18] certain other nonrecurring adjustments. We believe that, when considered together with reported GAAP amounts, Adjusted
[7:19] EBITDA is useful to investors and management in understanding our ongoing operations and ongoing operating trends. Our
[7:20] definition of Adjusted EBITDA may differ from the definition used by other companies and therefore comparability may be
[7:21] limited. Free cash flow represents the net cash and cash equivalents provided by operating activities less purchases of property,
[7:22] equipment, and intangible assets acquired through asset acquisitions. We believe that free cash flow is a useful indicator of our
[7:23] unit economics and liquidity that provides information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated from
[7:24] our core operations that, after the purchases of property, equipment, and intangible assets acquired through asset acquisitions,
[7:25] can be used for strategic initiatives.
[7:26]       Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations in their usefulness to investors because they have no standardized
[7:27] meaning prescribed by GAAP and are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. In addition,
[7:28] other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures differently
[7:29] or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial
[7:30] information as a tool for comparison. As a result, our non-GAAP financial information is presented for supplemental
[7:31] informational purposes only and should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for financial information
[7:32] presented in accordance with GAAP.
[7:33]        Reconciliation tables of the most comparable GAAP financial measure to the non-GAAP financial measure used in this
[7:34] press release are included below. We encourage investors and others to review our business, results of operations, and financial
[7:35] information in their entirety, not to rely on any single financial measure, and to view these non-GAAP measures in conjunction
[7:36] with the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures.

[1:4] SAN MATEO, Calif., October 31, 2024 - Roblox Corporation (NYSE: RBLX), a global platform bringing millions of people
[1:5] together through shared experiences, released its third quarter 2024 financial and operational results and issued its fourth
[1:6] quarter and updated full year 2024 guidance today. Separately, Roblox posted a letter to shareholders and supplemental
[1:7] materials on the Roblox investor relations website at ir.roblox.com.
[1:8] Third Quarter 2024 Financial, Operational, and Liquidity Highlights
[1:9]        •   Revenue was $919.0 million, up 29% year-over-year.
[1:10]        •   Bookings1 were $1,128.5 million, up 34% year-over-year.
[1:11]        •   Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $239.3 million, while consolidated net loss was $240.4 million.
[1:12]        •   Adjusted EBITDA1 was $55.0 million, which excludes adjustments for increases in deferred revenue and deferred cost
[1:13]            of revenue of $216.3 million and $(47.9) million, respectively, or a total change in deferred of $168.4 million.
[1:14]        •   Net cash and cash equivalents provided by operating activities was $247.4 million, up 120% year-over-year, while free
[1:15]            cash flow1 was $218.0 million, up 266% year-over-year.
[1:16]        •   Average Daily Active Users (“DAUs”) were 88.9 million, up 27% year-over-year.
[1:17]        •   Average monthly unique payers were 19.1 million, up 30% year-over-year, and average bookings per monthly unique
[1:18]            payer was $19.70.
[1:19]        •   Hours engaged were 20.7 billion, up 29% year-over-year.
[1:20]        •   Average bookings per DAU was $12.70, up 6% year-over-year.
[1:21]        •   Cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, and long-term investments totaled $3.9 billion; net liquidity2 was
[1:22]            $2.9 billion.
[1:23] “Roblox’s exceptional Q3 results demonstrate the strength of our platform and the effectiveness of our growth strategies. We’re
[1:24] particularly proud of the progress we’ve made in empowering creators, fostering social connections, and expanding our global
[1:25] reach. As we look ahead, we remain committed to building the world’s largest social platform for play, and we’re confident that
[1:26] our continued innovation and focus on safety will drive long-term value for our shareholders and the broader Roblox
[1:27] community,” said David Baszucki, founder and CEO of Roblox.
